youtube.title: Nokia's Burning Platform: The 2011 Bet on Windows Phone Over Android
youtube.description:
In 2007, Nokia sold about four in every ten mobile phones on Earth. Six years later, it sold its phone business to Microsoft for 5.44 billion euros. In between sits one memo, the "burning platform", and one decision: to bet everything on Windows Phone instead of Android or its own MeeGo.

This documentary goes into that February 2011 decision: the options on the table, why Microsoft looked like the safer road, and how announcing the end of Symbian before any replacement existed set off a chain that ran from profit warnings to job cuts to a sale. Every figure on screen comes from Nokia's own reports, Microsoft's filings and named research firms.

sources.claim: On 3 September 2013 Microsoft agreed to buy Nokia's phone business
sources.source: Microsoft and Nokia joint press release, 3 September 2013

sources.claim: The price was 5.44 billion euros: 3.79 billion for the Devices & Services business and 1.65 billion to license Nokia's patents
sources.source: Microsoft and Nokia joint press release, 3 September 2013

sources.claim: About 32,000 Nokia employees were expected to move to Microsoft
sources.source: Microsoft and Nokia joint press release, 3 September 2013

sources.claim: Nokia's estimated share of the world mobile device market in 2007 was about 40%
sources.source: Nokia Annual Report / Form 20-F for 2007, March 2008

sources.claim: Nokia shipped 437 million mobile devices in 2007
sources.source: Nokia Q4 and full-year 2007 report, 24 January 2008 (437.1 million)

sources.claim: Nokia's 2007 net sales were 51.1 billion euros and operating profit about 8 billion euros
sources.source: Nokia Annual Report 2007 (net sales EUR 51,058m; operating profit EUR 7,985m)

sources.claim: Nokia began in 1865 as a paper mill in Finland
sources.source: Nokia corporate history, nokia.com, 'Our history'

sources.claim: Nokia had been the world's largest phone maker since 1998
sources.source: Strategy Analytics, global handset vendor report for Q1 2012, April 2012

sources.claim: Nokia's headquarters were in Espoo, just outside Helsinki
sources.source: Nokia Annual Report / Form 20-F for 2007, March 2008 (registered office: Keilalahdentie 4, Espoo, Finland)

sources.claim: The iPhone went on sale in the United States on 29 June 2007
sources.source: Apple press release, 'iPhone Premieres This Friday Night', 25 June 2007

sources.claim: The first Android phone went on sale in October 2008
sources.source: T-Mobile USA press release on the T-Mobile G1, 23 September 2008; US availability 22 October 2008

sources.claim: Nokia shipped about 100 million smartphones in 2010
sources.source: Nokia Q4 and full-year 2010 report, 27 January 2011 (quarterly converged device volumes summed)

sources.claim: In February 2010 Nokia and Intel merged their Maemo and Moblin systems into MeeGo
sources.source: Nokia and Intel joint press release, 15 February 2010

sources.claim: In September 2010 Nokia named Stephen Elop, from Microsoft, as CEO, effective 21 September
sources.source: Nokia press release, 10 September 2010

sources.claim: Elop was the first chief executive from outside Finland
sources.source: Reuters, 'Nokia names Microsoft's Elop as CEO', 10 September 2010

sources.claim: At Microsoft he had run the Business Division, which included Office
sources.source: Nokia press release, 10 September 2010; Microsoft executive biography, 2010

sources.claim: In Q4 2010 Android phones shipped 32.9 million and Symbian 31.0 million, Android passing Symbian for the first time
sources.source: Canalys, smartphone market report, 31 January 2011

sources.claim: The memo opened with a man on a burning North Sea oil platform who jumped into the icy water and survived
sources.source: Stephen Elop, internal memo to Nokia staff, published in full by Engadget, 8 February 2011

sources.claim: "I have learned that we are standing on a burning platform."
sources.source: Elop memo, Engadget, 8 February 2011

sources.claim: "The first iPhone shipped in 2007, and we still don't have a product that is close to their experience."
sources.source: Elop memo, Engadget, 8 February 2011

sources.claim: "Android came on the scene just over 2 years ago, and this week they took our leadership position in smartphone volumes. Unbelievable."
sources.source: Elop memo, Engadget, 8 February 2011

sources.claim: Chinese makers produce a device faster than "the time that it takes us to polish a PowerPoint presentation"
sources.source: Elop memo, Engadget, 8 February 2011

sources.claim: "We thought MeeGo would be a platform for winning high-end smartphones. However, at this rate, by the end of 2011, we might have only one MeeGo product in the market."
sources.source: Elop memo, Engadget, 8 February 2011

sources.claim: "The battle of devices has now become a war of ecosystems"
sources.source: Elop memo, Engadget, 8 February 2011

sources.claim: "We poured gasoline on our own burning platform."
sources.source: Elop memo, Engadget, 8 February 2011

sources.claim: Windows Phone 7 went on sale in October 2010
sources.source: Microsoft press release, 11 October 2010; European availability 21 October 2010

sources.claim: A Google vice-president posted "Two turkeys do not make an eagle."
sources.source: Vic Gundotra, Google VP of engineering, post on Twitter, 6 February 2011, reported by Reuters and The Guardian, 7 February 2011

sources.claim: Android was already used by Samsung, HTC and Motorola
sources.source: Gartner, worldwide smartphone sales by vendor, Q4 2010, 9 February 2011

sources.claim: Nokia's chief executive said the concern with Android was the difficulty of differentiating within it
sources.source: Elop remarks at Nokia Capital Markets Day press conference, London, 11 February 2011, reported by Reuters and Bloomberg the same day

sources.claim: Nokia bought the map company Navteq in 2008 for 8.1 billion dollars
sources.source: Nokia press releases, 1 October 2007 (agreement) and 10 July 2008 (completion)

sources.claim: Nokia Maps would be at the heart of Microsoft's mapping services
sources.source: Nokia and Microsoft joint press release, 11 February 2011

sources.claim: The chief executive told reporters the deal's value to Nokia ran into billions
sources.source: Bloomberg and Reuters reports of the 11 February 2011 press conference

sources.claim: Nokia would help drive the future of Windows Phone
sources.source: Nokia and Microsoft joint press release, 11 February 2011

sources.claim: On 11 February 2011 in London, Nokia announced Windows Phone as its principal smartphone strategy
sources.source: Nokia and Microsoft joint press release, 11 February 2011

sources.claim: Symbian became a 'franchise platform'; MeeGo would ship one device and move to longer-term exploration
sources.source: Nokia and Microsoft joint press release, 11 February 2011

sources.claim: Nokia expected to sell about 150 million more Symbian devices
sources.source: Nokia Capital Markets Day, 11 February 2011, reported by Reuters the same day

sources.claim: Nokia shares fell 14 percent on 11 February 2011
sources.source: Reuters, Helsinki market report, 11 February 2011

sources.claim: The first Windows Phone Lumia was announced on 26 October 2011
sources.source: Nokia press release, Nokia World London, 26 October 2011

sources.claim: On 27 April 2011 Nokia moved Symbian work and about 3,000 staff to Accenture and planned about 4,000 job cuts by end of 2012
sources.source: Nokia press release, 27 April 2011

sources.claim: On 31 May 2011 Nokia abandoned its forecast for the second quarter
sources.source: Nokia stock exchange release, 31 May 2011

sources.claim: The MeeGo N9 was unveiled in June 2011 and not sold in the United States or Britain
sources.source: Nokia press release, 21 June 2011; Nokia statements reported by Reuters, June 2011

sources.claim: Nokia's 2011 net loss was 1.16 billion euros
sources.source: Nokia Q4 and full-year 2011 report, 26 January 2012

sources.claim: Samsung overtook Nokia as the world's biggest phone maker in Q1 2012
sources.source: Strategy Analytics, April 2012

sources.claim: Standard & Poor's cut Nokia's credit rating to junk in April 2012
sources.source: Standard & Poor's rating action, 27 April 2012, reported by Reuters

sources.claim: On 14 June 2012 Nokia announced up to 10,000 more job cuts
sources.source: Nokia press release, 14 June 2012

sources.claim: Nokia's 2012 net loss was 3.1 billion euros
sources.source: Nokia Q4 and full-year 2012 report, 24 January 2013

sources.claim: Nokia smartphone shipments: 28.3 million (Q4 2010), 19.6 million (Q4 2011), 6.6 million (Q4 2012)
sources.source: Nokia quarterly reports of 27 January 2011, 26 January 2012 and 24 January 2013

sources.claim: Lumia sales reached 8.8 million in Q3 2013
sources.source: Nokia Q3 2013 interim report, 29 October 2013

sources.claim: The memo's author moved to Microsoft to lead its devices business
sources.source: Microsoft press release, 3 September 2013; Microsoft announcement, 25 April 2014

sources.claim: The deal closed on 25 April 2014
sources.source: Microsoft press release, 25 April 2014

sources.claim: On 8 July 2015 Microsoft wrote down 7.6 billion dollars and announced up to 7,800 job cuts
sources.source: Microsoft press release and SEC Form 8-K, 8 July 2015

sources.claim: In May 2016 Microsoft sold its feature phone business for 350 million dollars and HMD Global licensed the Nokia name for phones
sources.source: Microsoft and HMD Global announcements, 18 May 2016

sources.claim: Microsoft ended support for Windows 10 Mobile on 10 December 2019
sources.source: Microsoft Lifecycle Policy, Windows 10 Mobile end of support notice

sources.claim: Nokia agreed to buy Alcatel-Lucent for 15.6 billion euros in April 2015
sources.source: Nokia press release, 15 April 2015

sources.claim: Nokia sold its HERE maps business for 2.8 billion euros in August 2015
sources.source: Nokia press release, 3 August 2015

sources.claim: Google agreed to buy Motorola Mobility for 12.5 billion dollars in 2011
sources.source: Google press release, 15 August 2011

sources.claim: Google sold Motorola to Lenovo in 2014 for about 2.91 billion dollars, keeping most patents
sources.source: Google and Lenovo announcements, 29 January 2014
